idiom_name: public outline method + private member functions
implementation_notes: The classic form maps one-to-one onto C++: the public method states the steps and private member functions implement them (cppreference: non-static member functions), so nothing has to be emulated. Keep the outline non-virtual and the steps private; if a step is meant as an override hook, make the outline a non-virtual wrapper around private virtual functions (the NVI split) instead of exposing a public virtual step. What replaces the classic structure in large translation units is the file-local helper: Abseil's tip 186 recommends a non-member function in an unnamed namespace over a private method whenever the step needs no member state, because the declaration leaves the header, the signature states every input and output, and the class API stays small. Prefer the member form when a step reads or writes several members, holds a lock, or must be overridden; prefer the free form for pure transformations. C++20 ranges/views express 'one level of abstraction' for data transformations as composable adaptor expressions rather than a statement outline - that is the Collection Pipeline sibling, not a variant of this pattern.
pitfalls: Private steps declared in the header grow the class declaration and its compile-time dependencies without adding interface meaning; steps that need no member state belong in the unnamed namespace of the .cc file instead.
A virtual step turns the outline into an inheritance contract that an override can violate; keep the outline non-virtual and the hooks private virtual (NVI), or make the steps non-virtual at all.
Free helpers that need member state force `friend` declarations or widened access - the helper signature is the signal that it should have been a member.

variants.name: Unnamed-namespace file-local helper functions
variants.idiom_name: unnamed-namespace non-member functions in the translation unit
variants.implementation_notes: Abseil tip 186 turns the outline into a translation-unit-local composition: the entry point stays a member (or a free function) and each step is a non-member function in an unnamed namespace of the .cc file, so the signature states every input and output, the header does not grow, and refactoring a step cannot affect another translation unit. Choose it for pure transformations and helpers that read no member state; move a step back into the class when it needs several fields, mutates state, or must hold a mutex. The two forms compile identically after inlining - the difference is API surface, review clarity and rebuild cost.
pitfalls: Never place an unnamed namespace in a header: every including translation unit gets its own copy of each helper, inflating symbols and confusing debuggers.
A helper that needs member state ends up taking a getter-built struct or a widening pile of accessors; that is the signal to move it back into the class as a private member.
